title: PSRC Method Included in Singapore Building Design Standard
body:
The PSRC (Prefabricated SRC) column method has been included as an independent chapter in BC4:2025, the Building and Construction Authority (BCA) of Singapore’s design guide for high-strength steel-concrete composite columns.

BC4:2025 is a fundamental design guide for all buildings constructed in Singapore. Based on Eurocode 4, it addresses design methods for composite columns incorporating high-strength steel and concrete.

Having recognized the safety, economic efficiency, and innovation of this method through a number of projects constructed using PSRC in Singapore, the BCA has established an entirely new chapter (Chapter 6) specifically for the method. It has also included a variety of PSRC application examples in the practical design guide, Example Calculations to the Requirement of BC4:2025.

As one of the leaders in OSC (Off-Site Construction), which is gaining attention as the construction industry’s next-generation trend, PSRC is being widely applied to semiconductor plants, data centers, and advanced manufacturing facilities, where demand is growing in the AI (artificial intelligence) era. In Singapore, it has been applied to the Hyundai Motor Group Innovation Center Singapore (HMGICS) and the JTC (Jurong Town Corporation) Logistics Hub. Notably, the JTC Logistics Hub was selected as BCA Project of the Year 2024 in the industrial category.

Singapore maintains some of the world’s most stringent construction and structural safety standards while actively embracing technological innovation, giving it significant influence over construction markets across Southeast Asia. This achievement is expected to substantially enhance the credibility of the PSRC composite column method not only in Southeast Asian markets, including Malaysia, Thailand, and Vietnam, but also in other overseas markets.
